pages.title: Introduction | Firecrawl
pages.text:
Firecrawl is the context API for AI agents. Search, scrape, and interact with the live web to get clean Markdown or structured data.

## Get started



### Build directly with the API

Scrape your first page now. No account or API key is required for this request.

cURL

```
# No API key needed to get started — add -H "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" for higher rate limits:
curl -s -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://firecrawl.dev",
    "formats": ["markdown", "html"]
  }'
```

Add an API key when you need higher limits. See the Python SDK, Node SDK, or API reference to build it into your application.

## Other ways to get started

### Install the Firecrawl CLI

One command installs the Firecrawl CLI, authenticates in your browser, and adds skills to every detected coding agent.

```
npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser
```

Restart your coding agent after setup so it can discover the new skills. See
CLI for the full setup.

### Set up with an agent

Provide your agent with this Firecrawl setup prompt, or see all MCP setup options.


**For AI agents:** Use llms.txt for an index of the documentation, or llms-full.txt for the full text.

### Build and test directly

## Get your API key

Create a free account for direct API access and higher limits

## Try it in the Playground

Test Firecrawl in the browser without writing code

---

## What can Firecrawl do?

## Search

Search the web and get full page content from results

## Scrape

Extract content from any URL as markdown, HTML, or structured JSON

## Interact

Continue working with any scraped page: click, fill forms, extract dynamic
content

### Why Firecrawl?

* **LLM-ready output**: Clean markdown, structured JSON, screenshots, and more.
* **Handles the hard stuff**: Proxies, anti-bot, JavaScript rendering, and dynamic content.
* **Reliable**: Built for production with high uptime and consistent results.
* **Fast**: Results in seconds, optimized for high throughput.
* **MCP Server**: Connect Firecrawl to any AI tool via the Model Context Protocol.

Bounty: 5,000 credit reward for solid feedback on Alexandria

To qualify, complete a high-signal interview (thoughtful, concrete use cases, etc) with our Firecrawl Feedback Assistant. Only takes a few minutes, can be stopped at any time, and is both human/agent-friendly (just paste the link into your agentic harness!). Haven’t used Alexandria yet? Your take still counts.

Start the interview

Include your email to be eligible. Interviews are reviewed for quality at the end of each week.

---

## Search

Search the web and get full page content from results in one call. See the Search feature docs for all options.

```
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

firecrawl = Firecrawl(
  # No API key needed to get started — add one for higher rate limits:
  # api_key="fc-YOUR-API-KEY",
)

results = firecrawl.search(
    query="firecrawl",
    limit=3,
)
print(results)
```

```
import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl';

const firecrawl = new Firecrawl({
  // No API key needed to get started — add one for higher rate limits:
  // apiKey: "fc-YOUR-API-KEY",
});

const results = await firecrawl.search('firecrawl', {
  limit: 3,
  scrapeOptions: { formats: ['markdown'] }
});
console.log(results);
```

```
# No API key needed to get started — add -H "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" for higher rate limits:
curl -s -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "firecrawl",
    "limit": 3
  }'
```

```
# Search the web
firecrawl search "firecrawl web scraping" --limit 5 --pretty
```

## Scrape

Scrape any URL and get its content in markdown, HTML, or other formats. See the Scrape feature docs for all options.

```
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

firecrawl = Firecrawl(
  # No API key needed to get started — add one for higher rate limits:
  # api_key="fc-YOUR-API-KEY",
)

# Scrape a website:
doc = firecrawl.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev", formats=["markdown", "html"])
print(doc)
```

```
import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl';

const firecrawl = new Firecrawl({
  // No API key needed to get started — add one for higher rate limits:
  // apiKey: "fc-YOUR-API-KEY",
});

// Scrape a website:
const doc = await firecrawl.scrape('https://firecrawl.dev', { formats: ['markdown', 'html'] });
console.log(doc);
```

```
# No API key needed to get started — add -H "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" for higher rate limits:
curl -s -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://firecrawl.dev",
    "formats": ["markdown", "html"]
  }'
```

```
# Scrape a URL and get markdown
firecrawl https://firecrawl.dev

# With multiple formats (returns JSON)
firecrawl https://firecrawl.dev --format markdown,html,links --pretty
```

## Interact

Scrape a page, then keep working with it: click buttons, fill forms, extract dynamic content, or navigate deeper. Describe what you want in plain English or write code for full control. See the Interact feature docs for all options.

```
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(
  # No API key needed to get started — add one for higher rate limits:
  # api_key="fc-YOUR-API-KEY",
)

# 1. Scrape Amazon's homepage
result = app.scrape("https://www.amazon.com", formats=["markdown"])
scrape_id = result.metadata.scrape_id

# 2. Interact — search for a product and get its price
app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Search for iPhone 16 Pro Max")
response = app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Click on the first result and tell me the price")
print(response.output)

# 3. Stop the session
app.stop_interaction(scrape_id)
```

pages.title: OAuth for apps | Firecrawl
pages.text:
Firecrawl runs an OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Your app sends the user to Firecrawl, the user signs in and picks a team, and your app gets an access token it can use on the Firecrawl REST API in place of an API key. Usage is billed to the team the user picked.
Each connection gets its own API key, created by Firecrawl and never shown to your app. The user can see and revoke the connection under Connected apps in Settings, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn’t affect it.

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead. OAuth is for users who bring their own Firecrawl account. To compare OAuth with API keys and MCP sign-in, see Authentication.

## Overview

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Registration endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register` |
| Resource (audience) | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | Required, `S256` only |
| Client authentication | `none` (public clients, no client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour, prefix `fco_` |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days, prefix `fcr_`, single use |

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `firecrawl:global` | Full access to the Firecrawl REST API on the chosen team, using that team’s credits. This is the default when `scope` is omitted. |
| `offline_access` | Tells the user on the consent screen that your app stays connected until they revoke it. Requires `firecrawl:global`. |

A token can do anything an API key on that team can do. Request only what you need and keep tokens on your server.

## Register your app

Your app needs a `client_id`. There are two ways to get one, and neither needs approval from Firecrawl.

* Dynamic Client Registration
* Client ID Metadata Document

Register once with RFC 7591 and store the `client_id` it returns.

```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "client_name": "Acme Builder",
    "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
    "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
  }'
```

The `client_name` is what users see on the consent screen.

Host a JSON metadata document at an HTTPS URL you control and use that URL as your `client_id`. Firecrawl fetches it during authorization, so you can update your name and redirect URIs without registering again. The consent screen shows the document’s host to the user.

```
{
  "client_id": "https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl-client.json",
  "client_name": "Acme Builder",
  "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}
```

Redirect URIs must use HTTPS. `http://localhost` and other loopback addresses are allowed for local development. A redirect URI may not contain a fragment or user info, and the URI you send at authorization must match a registered one exactly.

## Authorize

Generate a PKCE `code_verifier` and its S256 `code_challenge`, then send the user’s browser to the authorization endpoint.

```
https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.example%2Foauth%2Ffirecrawl%2Fcallback
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &scope=firecrawl%3Aglobal%20offline_access
  &resource=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.firecrawl.dev%2F
  &state=RANDOM_STATE
```

| Parameter | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_type` | Yes | Must be `code`. |
| `client_id` | Yes | From registration, or your metadata document URL. |
| `redirect_uri` | Yes | Must match a registered redirect URI. |
| `code_challenge` | Yes | Base64url SHA-256 of the `code_verifier`. |
| `code_challenge_method` | Yes | Must be `S256`. |
| `scope` | No | Space-separated. Defaults to `firecrawl:global`. |
| `resource` | No | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` for the REST API. This is the default. |
| `state` | Recommended | Returned unchanged. Check it on the callback. |

The user signs in if needed, chooses a team, and approves. Firecrawl then redirects to your `redirect_uri` with `code` and `state`. The code is valid for a short time and only once.
If the user cancels, Firecrawl redirects with `error=access_denied`.

## Exchange the code

```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d redirect_uri=https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback \
  -d resource=https://api.firecrawl.dev/
```

The token endpoint accepts `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or JSON.

```
{
  "access_token": "fco_...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "refresh_token": "fcr_...",
  "scope": "firecrawl:global offline_access",
  "user_id": "...",
  "team_id": "..."
}
```

`user_id` and `team_id` identify who authorized and which team is billed. Store both tokens server-side.

## Call the API

Send the access token as a bearer token, exactly like an API key.

```
curl -X POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fco_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'
```

The SDKs accept the token wherever they take an API key, for example `new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fco_..." })`.

## Refresh

Access tokens expire after one hour. Exchange the refresh token for a new pair before or after expiry.

```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=fcr_... \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
```

The response has the same shape as the code exchange. Refresh tokens rotate: each one works once, so always store the new `refresh_token` from the response. Using a refresh token a second time is treated as a stolen token: Firecrawl revokes the whole connection, including the tokens the first refresh just returned, and the user has to connect your app again. Serialize refreshes per connection and never retry a refresh that returned `invalid_grant`.

## Revoke

Call the revocation endpoint (RFC 7009) when the user disconnects Firecrawl in your app. Send the refresh token: that revokes the whole connection, including its access token and the key behind it. Sending an access token only invalidates that access token; the refresh token keeps working and the connection stays listed in the user’s Settings.

```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d token=fcr_...
```

The endpoint returns `200` even when the token is unknown or already revoked. Users can also revoke your app under Connected apps in Settings. A connection also ends when the authorizing user leaves the team.

## Errors

The authorization and token endpoints return standard OAuth errors as JSON: `{"error": "...", "error_description": "..."}`.


| Error | Endpoint | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | authorize, token | A required parameter is missing or malformed, for example no `code_challenge` or an unregistered `redirect_uri`. | Fix the request. |
| `invalid_client` | authorize | The `client_id` is unknown or its metadata document can’t be used. | Check registration. |
| `unsupported_response_type` | authorize | `response_type` isn’t `code`. | Use `code`. |
| `invalid_scope` | authorize, token | A scope isn’t supported, or `offline_access` was sent without `firecrawl:global`. | Request supported scopes. |
| `access_denied` | redirect | The user cancelled on the consent screen. | Let the user try again. |
| `invalid_grant` | token | The code or refresh token is invalid, expired, already used, or revoked; the PKCE verifier, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` or `resource` doesn’t match; or the user left the team. | Send the user through authorization again. |
| `unsupported_grant_type` | token | `grant_type` isn’t `authorization_code` or `refresh_token`. | Fix the request. |
| `server_error` | any | Temporary failure. | Retry with backoff. |

On the REST API, an OAuth token that is expired, revoked, or unknown gets `401` with `Unauthorized: Invalid or expired OAuth token`. Refresh once, and if that fails with `invalid_grant`, ask the user to reconnect. A `503` with `OAuth authentication is temporarily unavailable` is temporary; retry with backoff. Other errors, such as `402

pages.title: Authentication | Firecrawl
pages.text:
There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.

## Which should I use?

| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | API key | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in API keys. |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | Hosted MCP with an API key | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | MCP OAuth | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under Connected apps in Settings. |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | OAuth for apps | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead.
A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See No API key (keyless).

## API key

Create a key in the dashboard and send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY`. The SDKs take it as `apiKey`. A key has full access to the team that owns it, so keep it on your server. See Key restrictions to limit what a key can do.

## Hosted MCP with an API key

Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` and add the API key as a bearer token in the client config. Setup for each client is in Add an API key.

## MCP OAuth

Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`. The client opens a browser, the user signs in and picks a team, and Firecrawl creates a dedicated key for that connection. The client never sees the key. The native ChatGPT and Claude connectors use this flow automatically. Tokens from this flow work only on the MCP server, not on the REST API. See MCP sign-in.

## OAuth for apps

Send the user through Firecrawl’s OAuth flow with `resource=https://api.firecrawl.dev/`. Your app gets an `fco_` access token that works on the REST API in place of an API key, plus an `fcr_` refresh token.

* Each connection gets its own key. Your app never sees it, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn’t affect the connection.
* The connection is listed under Connected apps in Settings, where the user can revoke it.
* Refresh tokens rotate and work once. Reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole connection.

The full flow is in OAuth for apps.

## No API key (keyless)

These REST endpoints work without an API key:

* `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse` (including `/v2/parse/upload-url`)
* `/v2/scrape/{jobId}/interact`
* `/v1/scrape` and `/v1/search`
* On Firecrawl Cloud, the research, developer and government search endpoints

Every other endpoint, including crawl, map, extract, agent, batch scrape and job status, needs a key. Calling one without a key returns `401`.
To make a keyless request, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely. A header with an empty token, such as `Authorization: Bearer` with nothing after it, is rejected with `401 Unauthorized: Token missing`.

```
curl -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'
```

Keyless usage is free and limited per IP address. The limits vary with demand, and a `429` response means you’ve reached them. Sign up for a free API key to use every endpoint with higher limits. See Keyless (no API key) on the rate limits page.

pages.title: Introduction - Firecrawl Docs
pages.text:
## Features

## Scrape

Extract content from any webpage in markdown or json format.

## Crawl

Crawl entire websites, extract their content and metadata.

## Map

Get a complete list of URLs from any website quickly and reliably.

## Search

Search the web and get full page content in any format.

## Agentic Features

## Extract

Extract structured data from entire webpages using natural language.

## Base URL

All requests contain the following base URL:

```
https://api.firecrawl.dev
```

## Authentication

For authentication, include an `Authorization` header on every request except the keyless endpoints described below. The header should contain `Bearer fc-123456789`, where `fc-123456789` represents your API Key.

```
Authorization: Bearer fc-123456789
```

`/v1/scrape` and `/v1/search` also work without a key, with limits. To call them keyless, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely, because a header with an empty token returns `401`. See No API key (keyless) for the full list.
To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use OAuth for apps. Authentication compares every option.


## Response codes

Firecrawl employs conventional HTTP status codes to signify the outcome of your requests.
Typically, 2xx HTTP status codes denote success, 4xx codes represent failures related to the user, and 5xx codes signal infrastructure problems.


| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Request was successful. |
| 400 | Verify the correctness of the parameters. |
| 401 | The API key was not provided. |
| 402 | Payment required |
| 404 | The requested resource could not be located. |
| 408 | The request timed out (e.g., page took too long to load). |
| 429 | The rate limit has been surpassed. |
| 5xx | Signifies a server error with Firecrawl. |

Refer to the Error Codes section for a detailed explanation of all potential API errors.

### Firecrawl error codes

When a 408 or 5xx error occurs, Firecrawl provides more specific error codes to clarify what went wrong.


| Error Code | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCRAPE_TIMEOUT` | 408 | The page took too long to load or render. Try increasing the `timeout` parameter (up to 60000ms). |
| `SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED` | 500 | All scraping engines failed. |
| `SCRAPE_SSL_ERROR` | 500 | Page SSL certificate is invalid. You can use `skipTlsVerification:true` to bypass this check. |
| `SCRAPE_SITE_ERROR` | 500 | Unrecoverable site error. |
| `SCRAPE_DNS_RESOLUTION_ERROR` | 500 | DNS resolution failed. |
| `SCRAPE_ACTION_ERROR` | 500 | Error while performing a page action. |
| `SCRAPE_PDF_PREFETCH_FAILED` | 500 | Failed to prefetch PDF. |
| `SCRAPE_PDF_INSUFFICIENT_TIME_ERROR` | 500 | Not enough time to process PDF. |
| `SCRAPE_PDF_ANTIBOT_ERROR` | 500 | PDF blocked by anti-bot mechanisms. |
| `SCRAPE_ZDR_VIOLATION_ERROR` | 500 | Zero Data Retention conflict: occurs when `zeroDataRetention:true` but another option (e.g. `screenshot`) requires temporary storage. |
| `SCRAPE_UNSUPPORTED_FILE_ERROR` | 500 | Unsupported file type or file size exceeds 10MB limit. |
| `SCRAPE_LOCKDOWN_CACHE_MISS` | 404 | Lockdown mode is enabled but no cached data is available for the URL. Seed the cache with a non-lockdown scrape first, or disable `lockdown`. See Lockdown Mode. |
| `UNKNOWN_ERROR` | 500 | Generic or unexpected error. |

## 429 responses

When you exceed your plan’s rate or concurrency limits, the API returns a 429 response code. See Rate Limits for per-plan limits.
